newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Pharma Vision profit soars, good prospects.
newsitem.headline: Pharma Vision profit soars, good prospects.

text.p: Pharma Vision, one of the world's largest investment trusts specialised in the healthcare area, said 1996 net profit more than doubled to 393.1 million Swiss francs from 187.1 million and earnings prospects for companies in its portfolio looked good for the current year.

Pharma Vision, part of the BZ Group Holding that is chaired by financier Martin Ebner, also said in a statement that it added two new companies to its portfolio last year: Hoechst AG AG and U.S. genetic engineering company Tularik Inc., formed at the end of 1991.
The total value of Pharma Vision's portfolio of four participations was 5.2 billion francs at end-1996.
The profit on Pharma Vision's investments amounted to 612.9 million francs, up from 429.1 million.

Pharma Vision holds 15.6 percent of the bearer shares of Roche Holding AG, 10 percent of the common shares of Tularik, a 0.5 percent stake in Hoechst bearer shares and 0.2 percent of Glaxo Wellcome bearer shares.
While Pharma Vision's stake in Roche was reduced in 1996, Roche still accounts for 93.1 percent of its portfolio, down some five percentage points from the previous year.
The stake in Glaxo Wellcome accounts for 2.3 percent of Pharma Vision's participations while Hoechst accounts for 3.8 percent and Tularik for 0.8 percent.

Pharma Vision's confidence for this year is based on what it described as impressive product ranges at Roche and Glaxo Wellcome and a reorganisation of Hoechst that should bear fruit relatively quickly.

The most difficult outlook to evaluate for Pharma Vision is that of Tularik, although the quality of its management suggests that in a few years the company will be one of the most profitable in its portfolio, Pharma Vision said.
